newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Hebros Bank has 15 bln lev '96 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Hebros Bank has 15 bln lev '96 net profit.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Hebros Bank posted 15.4 billion levs net profit last year after a 255 million lev loss for 1995, an official said on Monday.
"An audit by Deloitte & Touche ascertained the bank had 15.384 billion lev net profit for 1996, which was transferred into its capital," a Deloitte & Touche official told reporters.
The Plovdiv-based bank's net worth totalled 1.416 billion levs at the end of 1996 after being negative the year before, the official added. He declined to elaborate.
The rise in the bank's net worth was due to the bank's recapitalisation through long-term domestic bad debt bonds worth $51 million in July and the sharp lev fall against the dollar last year.

"The seven-fold lev fall increased the net worth of Hebros Bank because around 63 percent of its assets were denominated in foreign currency and they strongly outweighed its dollar-denominated liabilities," the official said.

The bank's total assets rose from 197 billion levs at the end of 1996 to around 401 billion levs as of February 28 and it posted a net profit of 25.5 billion levs for the first two months under preliminary estimates, the bank's executive director Kostadin Iliev said.
The profit and the increase in assets were due to the sharp lev depreciation in the first two months, Iliev said.

The lev slumped to an all-time low of 3,200 per dollar on February 7 from around 600 at the beginning of the year before rebounding to around 2,000 per dollar at the end of February. It traded near 1,600 on Monday.

Hebros Bank's share capital totalled 10.4 billion levs at the end of February and its capital-to-risk assets ratio was 19.27 percent, Kostadin Iliev said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
